transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I'm here because... honestly, I just can't seem to leave work at work lately. We got a new operations manager recently, and they've started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. 

Ever since then, I just come home so wound up. I end up snapping at my husband, and I lie awake at night just... replaying the meetings in my head. Then the next day, I go in and I find myself second-guessing routine quality calls that I used to make without any trouble at all. It's just really getting to me.
Does this constant worrying focus mainly on your work situation, or do you find yourself worrying excessively about several other areas of your life as well?

It's really just work. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying about bills or my health or anything like that. My life outside the plant is usually pretty steady. It's just... this whole thing with the new manager and my inspection logs. That's really the only thing taking up all my headspace right now.
Aside from the stress and frustration about work, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless most days?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. I'm just incredibly frustrated and stressed out about this situation at the plant. It's not like a dark cloud over my whole life or anything, it's just this one specific thing that's making me so tense and on edge.
Did these feelings of stress and difficulty sleeping begin within three months of when the new manager started?

Yes, definitely. I was doing just fine before he came in. The trouble started building up within a few weeks of him changing our procedures. I'd say by the second month he was there, I knew my reactions to him were affecting me well beyond the workday.
